scope: Conceptual only, no render or actual-device evidence.

sceneChecks.name: A living trap, already active
sceneChecks.picture: Extreme macro of an open living-looking trap: inner lobe texture and a tiny moving subject or clearly identified illustrative probe. A hair begins bending while the opening names the plant and memory; no title card. Original illustrative biological scene, not unstated laboratory footage.
sceneChecks.development: Material detail and purposeful movement make the subject legible immediately. No need to conceal the answer with waiting.
sceneChecks.truth: Six trigger hairs across two lobes; larger marginal cilia are not trigger hairs. No natural visible calcium light.
sceneChecks.understanding: Memory can exist without a brain in a specific physiological sense.
sceneChecks.needsLaterEvidence: After explicit production authority, inspect actual opening/prototype mechanisms and the complete rendered sequence separately from technical QA.

sceneChecks.name: One brief stimulus, trap still open
sceneChecks.picture: Camera approaches one inner trigger hair, follows its brief deflection at the base, then reveals the open lobes. Choose an illustrative above-signal-threshold single-AP example; the probe/insect does not keep touching other hairs.
sceneChecks.development: A physical event is unmistakable while lack of snap creates the wanted difference.
sceneChecks.truth: The chosen brief movement is one possible response, not proof that every first physical touch creates exactly oneAP. No animal-neuron cables or lightning.
sceneChecks.understanding: External movement and internal signaling differ.
sceneChecks.needsLaterEvidence: After explicit production authority, inspect actual opening/prototype mechanisms and the complete rendered sequence separately from technical QA.

sceneChecks.name: The invisible response
sceneChecks.picture: A matched move from the hair base into a simplified tissue cutaway. A short electrical-signal cue is accompanied by a spreading calcium-activity tint in leaf tissue. Warm signal tint against natural greens; label it calcium activity • illustration throughout.
sceneChecks.development: Maintain spatial orientation from intact leaf to internal state instead of cutting to an unrelated slide.
sceneChecks.truth: Tint is qualitative relative activity, not emitted light, measured cells, moving calcium fluid, or a universal route via veins. Do not claim an exact AP/Ca propagation-speed relation.
sceneChecks.understanding: Calcium concentration changes inside cells as the trap is excited.
sceneChecks.needsLaterEvidence: After explicit production authority, inspect actual opening/prototype mechanisms and the complete rendered sequence separately from technical QA.

sceneChecks.name: A trace that fades
sceneChecks.picture: The moving signal cue passes; calcium tint remains and gradually weakens. A restrained time-compressed dissolve shows waiting without a stopwatch. Do not instantly zero the trace.
sceneChecks.development: Different persistence of brief excitation and residual biochemical state becomes the mechanism.
sceneChecks.truth: Decay has no fixed linear slope or30-second reset. Time compression and qualitative illustration are disclosed. Representative tissue, not a single identified memory cell.
sceneChecks.understanding: The retained state is temporary information about the earlier signal.
sceneChecks.needsLaterEvidence: After explicit production authority, inspect actual opening/prototype mechanisms and the complete rendered sequence separately from technical QA.

sceneChecks.name: A nearby signal builds on what remains
sceneChecks.picture: In the close-spacing example, another distinct electrical cue accompanies an increase on the remaining calcium tint. The tissue becomes more active; camera returns to the whole trap for a convincing snap. Keep a short level linked to closure cue if needed, with no numeric chart.
sceneChecks.development: Second response visibly starts from the elevated baseline, then resolves in the same living geometry.
sceneChecks.truth: Separate electrical events; model threshold is qualitative/probabilistic. Show one plausible closing example, not guaranteed closure for all plants or a mapped mechanical motor.
sceneChecks.understanding: Temporal accumulation can take a response into the closure-associated regime.
sceneChecks.needsLaterEvidence: After explicit production authority, inspect actual opening/prototype mechanisms and the complete rendered sequence separately from technical QA.

sceneChecks.name: Longer waiting changes the outcome
sceneChecks.picture: Cut clearly to a separate illustrative trial with a wider view. First response fades more; a later signal produces another rise that remains too low for closure in this example. The trap stays open. A compact separate example • time compressed cue prevents apparent instant reopening.
sceneChecks.development: The viewer compares outcomes using the same explanatory vocabulary without a permanent split-screen dashboard.
sceneChecks.truth: Do not reverse a snapped trap to reopen immediately or imply a complete reset at exactly30s. No universal delay cutoff; no new claim about reopening time.
sceneChecks.understanding: Timing changes how much residual state the next signal can build on.
sceneChecks.needsLaterEvidence: After explicit production authority, inspect actual opening/prototype mechanisms and the complete rendered sequence separately from technical QA.

sceneChecks.name: Signals are not touches
sceneChecks.picture: Extreme hair-base view in another clearly separate trial: one slower bend-and-return movement accompanies two distinct signal cues and a plausible closing response. Event cues remain visible briefly, without a dense calcium/AP chart.
sceneChecks.development: A concrete exception corrects the counting shortcut after the main mechanism is understood.
sceneChecks.truth: Slow movement within tested triggering conditions, not stationary holding. Both APs may occur on bending or on bending plus return; select the latter documented case. No claim each contact always gives twoAPs.
sceneChecks.understanding: A physical movement is not the unit being integrated.
sceneChecks.needsLaterEvidence: After explicit production authority, inspect actual opening/prototype mechanisms and the complete rendered sequence separately from technical QA.

sceneChecks.name: The memory is the trace
sceneChecks.picture: Return to natural light and the original open-trap illustrative trial after the first signal; briefly reveal its residual chemical state, then settle on the living leaf with biochemical memory as the only optional concluding label. No unmarked reopening or reset, no engagement outro.
sceneChecks.development: The ordinary-looking open trap now carries an understood internal history.
sceneChecks.truth: A clearly signaled return to the earlier example, not continuity from a freshly snapped trap. Memory is defined functionally and does not establish conscious experience.
sceneChecks.understanding: A past event persists as chemistry and can affect the next response.
sceneChecks.needsLaterEvidence: After explicit production authority, inspect actual opening/prototype mechanisms and the complete rendered sequence separately from technical QA.

retelling: A movement can create electrical signals; a signal accompanies a rise in calcium; some increase remains briefly and fades; later signals can add before decay; a sufficiently strong response is associated with closure. Two signals need not be two physical touches.
nonClaims: No one universal stopwatch or absolute-calcium cutoff.
No recorded physiological experiment in the planned original illustration.
No full anatomical or mechanical causal resolution.
No subjective comprehension pass from validated JSON.
